title: Narrow string reset to empty SSO
summary: Recovered Game.exe VA 0x48d630 (RVA 0x8d630), 166 bytes, as a genuine no-argument thiscall member on a 24-byte string: storage at +0, length at +16, unsigned capacity at +20. Resets length to zero, capacity to 15 and inline byte zero to NUL before releasing old heap storage through an explicit port integration hook. Capacity >=16 selects heap, including null allocation pointers. Direct original disassembly and embedded-string callers at 0x44f0e9, 0x48d89c and 0x56cc78 were inspected. Accepted reset, storage-swap, inline-swap, cookie-check and memcpy-import oracle bytes were independently compared to the immutable PE image and matched. This is readable semantic recovery, not a matching source build.
test_description: GCC i386 freestanding differential suite passed 108 cases and 216 original calls. Capacities 0,1,14,15,16,17,31,255,0x7fffffff,0x80000000,0xffffffff crossed with lengths 0,1,7,15,16,0xffffffff; heap cases additionally use null pointers. Checks empty result, exact delete count and argument, reset-before-delete ordering, unchanged neighboring fields and allocation contents, retained heap-storage bytes 1..15, one-byte memcpy import, and no double delete on repeated reset. Initializes test-owned FS storage, requires successful test_install_fs, and checks the constant original FS head after every original call. Controlled callbacks use exact four-byte .oracle_delete, .oracle_cookie and .test_iat fixtures. Oracle code is assembled only from accepted references and linked at original addresses; no original instructions are embedded in submitted C++.
known_limits: For originally inline strings, original swaps all 16 temporary storage bytes but initializes only byte zero. Bytes 1..15 receive unspecified stack residue; recovered C++ preserves these inactive bytes and tests intentionally do not compare them. Exact physical stack-residue reproduction is neither defined C++ nor claimed.

Normal return only: Windows SEH dispatch, exception unwinding, security-cookie failure and CRT internals are not recovered or validated. Original FS registration/restoration is exercised by the test runtime; portable implementation omits compiler runtime bookkeeping.
The delete integration hook must be supplied by the port with the corresponding allocation policy. Controlled callbacks establish import arguments and ordering, not actual allocator behavior.

Tests use writable disjoint objects and readable 16-byte inline storage; invalid addresses and aliasing the callee's private temporary are outside the recovered contract. Deliberately inconsistent metadata demonstrates branch behavior, not validity as a general string.

Original ABI and differential testing are i386. The readable implementation uses C++11-compatible syntax for MSVC2013, but the optional pinned MSVC tool was unavailable in this sandbox. No source-byte matching credit is claimed.
